title: Welded plate box
description: A rectangular box, cube or beam of laser-cut steel plate from 3 mm up, as a building block for machines. The plates meet in plain contact, and short tabs whose ends stand below the mating face hold the weld. Half-lapped internal ribs slide into an egg-crate, and enter the walls with the same tabs. Tab and slot from the laser hold the box straight and square while it is welded; weld distortion is not predicted, so keep the tabs short and follow the weld sequence in the README. Openings per pair of walls, sized by the wall: rectangles, rounded rectangles, circles or a truss of triangles. Outputs: mass, plate list, weld length and share, and the stiffness of the section. This Jig gives no strength figures and does not say what the box can carry: whoever builds a machine frame from it must have the frame and its welds checked by a qualified person. Export each plate as DXF or SVG with File > Export, Sheet of set: Cut: top and bottom, Cut: front and back, Cut: left and right, Cut: ribs, first and second family; STEP exports the whole box.
